newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges fraud in PanWorld stock sales.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges fraud in PanWorld stock sales.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Wednesday it filed fraud charges against PanWorld Minerals International Inc., its top executive, several affiliated consultants and a radio talk show host, alleging they illegally lured investors into spending $9.4 million to purchase millions of shares of the company.

"The main fraud that occurred here is that the company and its insiders were hyping the stock and at the same time they were dumping their shares," Robert Fusfeld, the SEC attorney handling the case, told Reuters.

The agency, in its complaint filed Monday in U.S. District Court in Utah, alleged the company's chief executive officer and two other individuals who controlled the Salt Late City mining company spearheaded the scheme.
Fusfeld said PanWorld is not actively in business anymore nor are its shares traded publicly.
In its complaint, the SEC said CEO Robert Weeks, 55, consultant David Hesterman, 40, and consultant Kenneth Weeks, 41, prepared false periodic reports that were filed with the SEC.
The men also were accused of distributing promotional materials to investors and broker-dealers that inflated the value of the company's mineral properties.
"They weren't anywhere near as valuable as they claimed to be," the SEC's Fusfeld said. "All the company really was doing was selling stock."

Fusfeld said more than 1,000 investors were swayed into buying nearly 500 million of shares of the company after receiving inflated and misleading information disclosed in marketing materials, public documents and even in a radio broadcast.

At the time, the defendents were making these false statements, which were designed to give the impression that PanWorld was an active and profitable company, Fusfeld said they also solicited a network of consultants to "fraudulently tout" PanWorld stock.

The SEC alleged these consultants, who were also named in the complaint, were issued stock as payment for their services of promoting the company and its shares. Named as one of these consultants in the complaint was Jerome Wenger, 51, of Bethesda, Maryland, who hosts The Next SuperStock radio show, a nationally broadcast program.
